scores.evidence: Each of the six views opens with a one-line question as its title (e.g. 'How does a submitted task reach a slot and return its result?') and names the audience ('Engineers onboarding to offstage and offstage cloud') with a scope line. The amount of detail (routes, timeouts, lanes) suits onboarding engineers.

Every box is a runtime component (CLI, classifier, lanes, plane API, queue, store, fleetd, slot, SaaS), and none of them mix in code symbols or teams. View 1 is the overview and views 2–6 zoom into workflows A–E, so the zoom-in condition is met. Folding the queue into the plane in the overview is a deliberate simplification.

The core paths are covered. However, the deliberate omissions (billing, mail, site/, launch/, bench/) appear only in the map JSON and are not stated anywhere visible, so they earn no credit. Some hops are missing: in view 6 (titled '...reach the fleet') no edge shows the job going from the plane through fleetd to the slot; E3 just appears. In view 5, nothing shows how a D1 agent run gets to the slot. The overview leaves out the local lanes, even though the title promises both halves.

Views 2–6 have numbered, labelled, directed calls marked sync/local/async, and the legend says 'Caller → recipient; response included.' View 1 breaks this. The fleetd→plane 'long-poll claim → work' label and the 'submit task, wait' label are not visible (two SDK→plane edges collapse into one), and the dotted fleetd→slot edge is drawn starting inside the Control plane API box, so it reads as plane→slot. In view 5, C1/C2 are drawn below D1–D3, which muddles the ordering.

Views 2–6 have clear headed containers with descriptions: 'Fly.io offstage-api — exla-operated…managed', 'Developer console account…self-hosted', 'Customer browser / code — not run by exla', 'Third-party SaaS', and the operator and slot accounts on the fleet Mac. View 1, the entry view, has no containers at all, only subtitles under node names, even though its legend says 'Headers = boundaries'.

Views 3–6 are tidy left-to-right sequence layouts with few crossings. View 1 has a dotted edge running through the plane node and a label hidden behind it ('…ocal)'), plus missing labels. Group descriptions and edge labels in views 2, 5 and 6 are about 9–11 px at 1194x834 and hard to read. Readable, but awkward in the entry view.

Every view has a visible legend: solid line = sync request, dotted = local I/O, dashed = async delivery, cylinder = store, faint guides = actors, headers = boundaries, and 'unnumbered calls are independent'. Real names (Clerk, Anthropic API, GitHub App / Actions, fleetd, sessiond) are used, external systems are marked '(external)', and line style plus text carry meaning without relying on colour.

These are visible: the 20 s claim ack with requeue up to 3 attempts, quota → 429, a 25 s long-poll, 'Refuse beats route' and no fallback to the console, reset retried with backoff, Clerk unreachable → 502 / bad token → 401, a JSON snapshot every 2 s, the single Fly machine with /data, and the run token keeping the key off the slot. Not visible: the in-memory queue on a single machine as a single point of failure (a failed snapshot write is only logged), BOX_LOST_MS, and an owner ('Unassigned').

The footer shows 'Source review 2026-11-05 · 57eeabc + local edits · Owner: Unassigned · Live runtime NOT verified'. Constants match the code: CLAIM_ACK_MS=20_000, MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 (cloud/src/core/store.ts), MAX_POLL_MS=25_000 (queue.ts), and a 2_000 ms snapshot interval (server.ts:106-112). Routes /v1/tasks, ?wait=, /v1/model/messages and generate-jitconfig, the oc_session cookie, and Clerk 401/502 also match. Capped at 3 because there is no live verification.

With views 2–6, a newcomer can explain the local lane routing and the cloud pull model correctly. The overview, though, could mislead them into thinking the plane pushes work straight to slots. They also can't see how GitHub jobs and agent runs actually reach a slot, so a short walkthrough would still help.

coldRead: offstage has two halves. Locally (view 2), the offstage CLI/MCP on a developer's account asks the Route classifier to pick a lane for a command, or to refuse it if it's an installer, .dmg or .pkg. It then either spawns the command in place (headless lane), runs it in a Docker container on Xvfb (container lane), or sends it over a Unix socket to a Swift sessiond inside a second logged-in macOS helper account (session lane). It never falls back to the real screen. In the cloud (views 1, 3–6), customers use the SDK or web console to call a Hono control plane on a single Fly.io machine. Tasks are quota-checked into an in-memory queue that is snapshotted to a /data volume every 2 s. fleetd on a fleet Mac only makes outbound calls: it long-polls for claims and sandbox ops (≤25 s), must ack a claim within 20 s (or the task is requeued, up to 3 tries), runs the work as a slot user (offstage0–7) through sessiond or sudo -u, posts events and artifacts back, and recreates a dirty slot account before its next claim. For computer-use runs, the slot's agent calls the plane's model proxy with a run token, and the plane calls Anthropic with the customer's key. GitHub sends workflow_job webhooks, the plane requests a JIT runner config, and an Actions runner in a slot runs the job. Console sign-in goes through Clerk, which the plane verifies server-side.
inaccuracies: View 5, edge D1 reads 'POST /sandboxes/:id/agent', but the route is POST /v1/sandboxes/:id/agent (cloud/src/api/agent-routes.ts:117). The other labels (B1 /v1/tasks, D2 /v1/model/messages) keep the /v1 prefix.

View 1 draws the dotted fleetd→slot 'run as slot user' edge starting inside the Control plane API box, so it reads as the plane calling the slot directly. In the code the plane never calls a slot: fleetd pulls work and runs it in the slot (src/fleet/runner.ts, src/fleet/slot-executor.ts), which the view's own 'Pull model, no inbound ports' note says too.
improvements: Re-lay out view 1 so the fleetd→slot edge doesn't pass through the plane node, show the hidden 'long-poll claim → work' and 'submit task, wait' labels, and add the same boundary containers (Fly.io plane, fleet Mac operator, slot accounts, customer) that views 2–6 use.

Fill in the missing hops: in view 6, show the GitHub job going from the plane through fleetd's claim to the slot before E3; in view 5, show how a D1 agent run reaches the slot (an op or claim through fleetd). Order C/D so the sequence reads top to bottom.

Show the omissions and the state/failure note on the canvas: list what's left out (billing, mail, site/, launch/, bench/), state that the queue is in memory on one Fly machine (a crash loses up to 2 s, a failed snapshot write is only logged) and that a box unheard for 2 min loses its work, and enlarge the 9–11 px group descriptions and edge labels.
